name: Tax Structuring and Planning
title: Tax Structuring and Planning
answer: Tax structuring and planning is the practice of arranging a company's legal entities, transactions, and cash flows so that tax outcomes follow the commercial substance and the applicable rules. It covers entity choice, holding company location, financing, intellectual property ownership, transfer pricing, treaty access, credits, and incentives. It is not tax evasion, which is illegal, and it is not a single product; it is a set of decisions made with advisers and documented for auditors. The work sits inside tax and jurisdictional compliance, part of The AI Accountant.

sections.body: Tax structuring and planning is the practice of arranging a company's legal entities, transactions, and cash flows so that tax outcomes follow the commercial substance and the applicable rules. It covers entity choice, holding company location, financing, intellectual property ownership, transfer pricing, treaty access, credits, and incentives. It is not tax evasion, which is illegal, and it is not a single product; it is a set of decisions made with advisers and documented for auditors. The work sits inside tax and jurisdictional compliance, part of The AI Accountant.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Tax structuring runs on the same systems that hold legal entity data, ownership charts, intercompany agreements, invoices, and ledger entries. In practice that means ERP and consolidation systems, tax provision and compliance software, transfer pricing databases, and document management for rulings and opinions. Increasingly it also runs on data pipelines that feed AI models for entity classification, invoice coding, and risk scoring. The quality of the structure analysis depends on the quality of the underlying data, so reconciliation between legal, finance, and tax records is a core infrastructure concern.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners start with the facts: who does what, where people work, where risks are taken, and where value is created. They map those facts to the relevant tax rules, model scenarios, and test the structure against transfer pricing and anti-avoidance provisions. Documentation is prepared as the structure is built, not after, because tax authorities expect contemporaneous evidence. AI can assist with document review, data extraction, and anomaly detection, but the judgment and the signature remain with qualified tax professionals.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Tax structuring carries legal, reputational, and financial risk, and the line between acceptable planning and abusive avoidance is drawn by statute, case law, and administrative practice. Provenance matters: every assumption, advice, and calculation is expected to be traceable to a source, a date, and a responsible person. Where AI is used, the model's inputs, training data, and outputs are documented so that a reviewer can reconstruct the reasoning. The atlas tracks 222 compliance and regulation pages, which is the natural place to check current rules and reporting duties.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Tax structuring is moving toward more real-time data, more automated reporting, and more scrutiny of cross-border arrangements. Digital tax administration, including e-invoicing and country-by-country reporting, is making structures more visible to authorities. AI is likely to shift the work from manual document review toward pattern detection and scenario simulation, while human advisers focus on judgment and negotiation. The direction is not less planning but more documented, data-backed planning that can withstand review.
